task.title: intcomma groups floats of 1e16 and above, and tiny floats, instead of printing exponents
task.body:
Why: https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/issues/431 ; src/humanize/number.py:206-208 uses f"{value:,}", which switches to exponent notation. On b519e48 `intcomma(1e16)` returns '1e+16', `intcomma(1.5e20)` returns '1.5e+20' and `intcomma(0.00001)` returns '1e-05'.
Outcome: `humanize.intcomma(value, ndigits=None)` with a finite float never returns exponent notation when `ndigits` is None. The float is written in fixed notation from its shortest repr digits, thousands grouped, and a whole-number float keeps the trailing '.0': `intcomma(1e16) == '10,000,000,000,000,000.0'`, `intcomma(1.5e20) == '150,000,000,000,000,000,000.0'`, `intcomma(1e22) == '10,000,000,000,000,000,000,000.0'`, `intcomma(0.00001) == '0.00001'`, `intcomma(-1.5e16) == '-15,000,000,000,000,000.0'`. Existing results stay: `intcomma(1e15) == '1,000,000,000,000,000.0'`, `intcomma(1234567.25) == '1,234,567.25'`, `intcomma(1e16, 0) == '10,000,000,000,000,000'`, `intcomma(1000) == '1,000'`, and locale separators still apply.
Proof: add tests to tests/test_number.py.
